language.script_notes: Indonesian as national; Javanese is the dominant regional language, occasionally appearing decoratively in its own script on cultural signage though rarely on road signs.
false_friends: Bali (shares some volcanic terrain and Javanese-origin temple architecture)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: As national; more substantial on the dense Java-wide highway network (the most developed in Indonesia).
road_furniture.curb_style: As national; denser, more developed urban infrastructure than most of the rest of the archipelago given Java holds the majority of Indonesia's population.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national. Toll road (tol) signage is far more extensive here than elsewhere in Indonesia.

architecture.roof_style: Steep, multi-tiered pyramidal roofs on traditional Javanese mosques — a strong regional architectural signature.
architecture.wall_construction: Dense, often informal urban development in and around Jakarta/Surabaya/Bandung; traditional joglo (Javanese pendopo-style) wooden houses with pyramidal roofs in rural/cultural areas.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Muted concrete/painted-block tones in cities; natural wood tones on traditional joglo houses.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Multi-tiered pyramidal-roofed mosques with ceremonial gateways; joglo traditional houses; dense informal Jakarta/Surabaya urban sprawl; ancient Hindu-Buddhist temple complexes (Borobudur, Prambanan).

nature.vegetation: Rice paddies terracing volcanic slopes; tropical vegetation intermixed with dense agricultural land — Java is Indonesia's most intensively farmed and populated island.
nature.terrain: Almost entirely of volcanic origin, with numerous active volcanoes forming a spine down the island; the most densely populated and developed island in the archipelago.
nature.climate_signature: Tropical, with volcanic peaks frequently visible on the horizon — Java's volcano-and-rice-terrace combination is a strong regional signature.

vehicles.plate_color: As national — Jakarta uses the 'B' area code.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Extremely heavy motorbike traffic, especially in Jakarta; the highest vehicle density in Indonesia given the population concentration.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Best and most complete coverage in Indonesia, concentrated around Jakarta, Surabaya, Bandung and Yogyakarta.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: By far the densest Street View coverage of any Indonesian island — most 'generic Indonesia' imagery is actually Java.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Volcanic terrain, rice terraces, shared Hindu-influenced temple architectural roots (Bali's temples descend from Javanese Hindu tradition)
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Java is predominantly Muslim with pyramidal-roofed mosques as the dominant religious architecture; Bali is predominantly Hindu with distinctive split-gate temples and meru towers — a strong differentiator.
Java is denser, more developed and volcano-studded with rice terraces; Sumatra is dominated by dense rainforest and has the distinctive curved-roof rumah gadang architecture Java lacks.
